headline: Dry into next week after the midweek storm's 8 inches
verdict: No snow in the NWS forecast for the Aspen area through Thursday, with highs in the mid-40s to mid-50s from Sunday. Keystone and A-Basin are open; Breckenridge and Copper plan to open today.
brief: The post-election rally reversed hard: the S&P 500 had its worst day since April 2025 as AI and chip stocks sold off. Asia followed, Brent neared $100 and October payrolls land at 6:30am MT.

lead.head: AI fears turn the midterm rally into a global rout
lead.text: The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Dow 1,833 points on Thursday, leaving the Nasdaq Composite down 5.5% and in correction, as investors bet a Democratic Congress will slow data-centre buildouts. Euro Stoxx 50 futures pointed about 1% lower before Friday's open.

markets.text: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.25% and the Nasdaq-100 6.3%, about $2.3 trillion of value, with SpaceX and Tesla down more than 9%.
Brent rose 1.6% to $99.90 on Friday morning as US–Iran uncertainty kept a floor under prices.

world.text: Ukrainian drones set fires in Ryazan, including at its Rosneft refinery, while Russia struck a Nova Poshta delivery hub near Kharkiv.
US, Ukrainian and Russian negotiators resume technical talks next week; Poland warned allies not to settle terms without Eastern Europe.
Israel's Arab-led Joint List will back Gadi Eisenkot to form a government, giving him an expected 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
Paraguay's Congress rejected President Santiago Peña's resignation, offered after the collapse of Ueno Bank.

us.text: Meta's president said the Democratic wins will make data centres harder to build and expects more projects to face local review.
UBS notes that Democratic control of the Senate means the President's Federal Reserve nominees now need Democratic votes.
Google, Meta and TikTok sued to block California's law curbing addictive feeds for under-16s, which takes effect on 1 January 2027.
Trump posted that stocks had one of their worst days ever but would recover.

economy.text: October payrolls are expected at +65,000 after +29,000, with unemployment at 4.2%; Michigan consumer sentiment follows.
The New York Fed's Williams called the economy resilient and said it is time to gather information; markets price 72.3% odds of a hike.
Eurozone retail sales fell 0.7% in September from August, against expectations of a 0.1% dip.

europe.text: At least 575,000 people marched across France on Thursday against the cost of living, the Interior Ministry said; 448 were arrested.
Bomb hoaxes disrupted at least 27 flights across Europe on Thursday; the EU says it is too early to say whether they are linked.

companies.text: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to buy AI-agent security startup Clutch for $500 million in cash, about 50 times its annual revenue.
Dropbox will pay $350 million for Tigris Data, apparently its largest acquisition, to build storage for AI agents.
Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation as Walmart agreed to add 300 US drone delivery sites.
AppLovin's third-quarter revenue of $2.18 billion beat the $2.07 billion expected, and it guided the fourth quarter to $2.37–2.40 billion.

financials.text: The first equity trades under the SEC's Innovation Exemption settled atomically on the Canton Network, with DRW Cumberland buying tokenised stock.
Bitcoin briefly fell below $76,000 on Thursday, down more than 5% on the day.

tech.text: OpenAI released ChatGPT Cyber to its top-tier security researchers after its models flagged 948 potential issues in the Linux kernel.
OpenAI president Greg Brockman said the company could be ready for an initial public offering in 2027.
Meta opened video chat with its Muse AI agent to all US users, ahead of a Muse wearable due before year-end.
Airbnb says it will launch an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027.

asia.text: The Nikkei fell as much as 7% and the Kospi 8.8%, tripping a halt; SK Hynix lost about 10% and TSMC up to 8.5%.
Seoul cut margin requirements for three months, Taiwan told regulators to prepare stabilisation steps and Japan floated support payments for workers.

mideast.text: Trump said the US may have to destroy the rest of Iran; Tehran reportedly sent a nuclear proposal through Qatar with conditions.
Iranian forces said at least five tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, several after striking mines.
Axios reports US Central Command is finalising preparations for possible renewed major combat, with no order yet issued.

science.text: Researchers who inject concepts into language models find the models can sometimes detect the tampering; whether that counts as introspection is disputed.

week.text: US October payrolls and Michigan sentiment; Canada jobs.
COP31 opens in Antalya; France's prime minister meets unions on wages.
US October CPI and real earnings at 6:30am MT.
Veterans Day, no BLS releases; COP31 leaders' summit opens.
US, Ukraine and Russia resume technical talks in Abu Dhabi.
